transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, we have a shipment of 600 drums of moisture-sensitive polyurethane adhesive that arrived this morning and is currently on hold due to a receiving temperature alarm. Friday's production schedule is going to need adhesive from this shipment or an approved replacement, so we need to work through this efficiently. Let's go through our standard receiving huddle review. I'd like to hear from quality, maintenance, logistics, and environmental health and safety on any relevant findings before we make a disposition decision. What are we seeing?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed my review of the temperature logger this morning. Exactly 72 drums exceeded the approved 8°C exposure limit for 90 minutes, so those 72 drums need to remain quarantined. The remaining 528 drums stayed within specification, and quality procedure permits those 528 drums for release. I haven't entered the result in the warehouse hold record yet.

transcript.text: I have an important update for the group. I confirmed with the adhesive supplier today that exactly 72 replacement drums will arrive Thursday at 15:00, and the 72 exposed drums need to be returned on the supplier's collection booking. I received this confirmation by email today but I have not yet logged either booking in the shipment tracker.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag an EHS storage requirement before any drums are released into storage. My storage review today found that this polyurethane adhesive must be placed in Cage 3 on grounded spill pallets, and an electrical grounding verification must be completed before any drum is released into storage. I recorded this requirement during my EHS review, but the storage map has not been updated yet, so I want to make sure everyone is aware before we proceed.
